Controls how two images are blended toge: Controls how two images are blended together. Low values (e.g. 0.5) produce uneven blending where one image dominates. A value of 1.0 gives any blend ratio equal chance. Higher values (e.g. 1.5-3.0) favour an equal 50/50 mix of both images.
Controls the DEIM multi-stage augmentati: Controls the DEIM multi-stage augmentation scheduling framework. When enabled, training uses complex multi-stage augmentations that automatically transition between strong and light augmentation phases during training. This may lead to better accuracy but increases training time. When disabled, a simpler static augmentation pipeline is used instead, allowing direct control over individual augmentations. WARNING: when the DEIM framework is enabled, all other augmentation parameters below are ignored and will have no effect on training. Note: the DEIM framework is not supported when tiling is enabled and will be automatically disabled in that case.
Data augmentation is a technique used in: Data augmentation is a technique used in machine learning to artificially expand a training dataset by applying transformations (e.g., rotation, scaling, noise) to existing data. It improves model generalization and reduces overfitting by increasing data variability without collecting new samples.
Early stopping is a technique to prevent: Early stopping is a technique to prevent overfitting by stopping training when performance on a validation set stops improving.
Factor by which the learning rate will b: Factor by which the learning rate will be reduced. new_lr = lr * factor.
Factor controlling the strength of the s: Factor controlling the strength of the sharpness adjustment. A value of 0.0 means no sharpening, higher values increase the effect. Typical values are between 0.0 and 1.0.
Fill value for the area outside the imag: Fill value for the area outside the image when zooming out. Typically 0 for black padding. Value should be between 0 and 255.
Fill value for the erased region, normal: Fill value for the erased region, normalized to [0, 1]. A value of 0.0 fills with black. A value of 1.0 fills with white.
Filtering parameters define criteria for: Filtering parameters define criteria for including or excluding annotations from the dataset. Depending on the scenario, an appropriate filter configuration can speed up the training process and/or improve the model performance by removing noisy annotations.
Gradient accumulation allows simulating: Gradient accumulation allows simulating larger batch sizes by accumulating gradients over multiple forward/backward passes before updating the model weights.
Gradient clipping prevents exploding gra: Gradient clipping prevents exploding gradients by capping gradient norms during backpropagation.
Height size in pixels for model input im: Height size in pixels for model input images. Determines the vertical resolution at which images are processed.
Intensity mapping parameters control how: Intensity mapping parameters control how raw pixel values are normalised to [0, 1] range before training. This is especially important for images with non-standard bit depths (e.g. 16-bit), where the default [0, 255] assumption does not hold.
Learning rate for the optimizer, control: Learning rate for the optimizer, controlling the step size during model weight updates. A smaller learning rate may lead to more stable convergence, while a larger learning rate may speed up training but risk overshooting minima in the loss landscape.
Learning rate warmup is a technique wher: Learning rate warmup is a technique where the learning rate starts at a lower value and gradually increases to the initial learning rate over a specified number of epochs at the beginning of training. This can help stabilize training and improve convergence, especially when using large learning rates or training on complex datasets.
List of supported values for input width: List of supported values for input width and height.
Maximum L2 norm of the gradients. Gradie: Maximum L2 norm of the gradients. Gradients with norm larger than this value will be clipped.
Maximum absolute shear angle in degrees: Maximum absolute shear angle in degrees to apply during affine transformation. A random shear in the range [-max_shear_degree, max_shear_degree] will be applied.
Maximum fraction of the original image a: Maximum fraction of the original image area to retain after cropping. A value of 1.0 means the crop can be as large as the entire image.
Maximum number of epochs to train the mo: Maximum number of epochs to train the model. An epoch is one complete pass through the training dataset.
Maximum number of objects in an annotati: Maximum number of objects in an annotation
Maximum output value after rescaling the: Maximum output value after rescaling the image in 'Range scaling with clipping' mode; pixel values above this threshold are clipped.
Maximum possible pixel value in the raw: Maximum possible pixel value in the raw image, used as the divisor for 'Unit interval scaling'. For 8-bit images use 255, for 16-bit images use 65535.
Maximum rotation angle in degrees for af: Maximum rotation angle in degrees for affine transformation. A random angle in the range [-max_rotate_degree, max_rotate_degree] will be applied. For example, max_rotate_degree=10 allows up to ±10 degrees rotation.
Maximum translation as a fraction of ima: Maximum translation as a fraction of image width or height. A random translation in the range [-max_translate_ratio, max_translate_ratio] will be applied along both axes. For example, 0.1 allows up to ±10% translation.
Mean of the Gaussian noise to be added t: Mean of the Gaussian noise to be added to the image. Typically set to 0.0 for zero-mean noise.
Metric used to evaluate model performanc: Metric used to evaluate model performance during validation.
Minimum fraction of the original image a: Minimum fraction of the original image area to retain after cropping. For example, 0.3 means the crop will be at least 30% of the original area.
Minimum number of objects in an annotati: Minimum number of objects in an annotation
Minimum number of pixels in an annotatio: Minimum number of pixels in an annotation
Minimum output value after rescaling the: Minimum output value after rescaling the image in 'Range scaling with clipping' mode; pixel values below this threshold are clipped.
Multiplicative factor applied to pixel v: Multiplicative factor applied to pixel values, before clipping the result to [clip_min_value, clip_max_value].
Number of epochs for the LR linear warmu: Number of epochs for the LR linear warmup phase.
Number of epochs with no improvement aft: Number of epochs with no improvement after which learning rate will be reduced.
Number of epochs with no improvement after which training will be stopped.
Number of steps (batches) to accumulate: Number of steps (batches) to accumulate gradients before performing gradient descent step. Effective batch size during training: batch_size * accumulate_grad_batches.
Number of training samples processed bef: Number of training samples processed before the model's internal parameters are updated. A larger batch size can speed up training but may require more memory, while a smaller batch size can help avoid OOM (Out of Memory) errors at the cost of longer training times and potentially noisier gradient estimates.
Overlap between adjacent tiles as a frac: Overlap between adjacent tiles as a fraction of tile size
Percentage of data to use for testing: Percentage of data to use for testing
Percentage of data to use for training: Percentage of data to use for training

Probability of applying Gaussian blur. A: Probability of applying Gaussian blur. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be blurred.
Probability of applying Gaussian noise. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to have noise added.
Probability of applying IoU random crop. A value of 1.0 means the crop is always applied when enabled.
Probability of applying color jitter. A: Probability of applying color jitter. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be color jittered.
Probability of applying horizontal flip. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be flipped horizontally.
Probability of applying mosaic augmentat: Probability of applying mosaic augmentation. A value of 1.0 means mosaic is always applied when enabled.
Probability of applying random erasing. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to have a region erased.
Probability of applying random zoom out. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be zoomed out.
Probability of applying sharpness adjust: Probability of applying sharpness adjustment. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be sharpened.
Probability of applying the affine trans: Probability of applying the affine transformation. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be transformed.
Probability of applying vertical flip. A: Probability of applying vertical flip. A value of 0.5 means each image has a 50% chance to be flipped vertically.
Probability of converting the image to g: Probability of converting the image to grayscale. A value of 0.1 means each image has a 10% chance to be converted to grayscale.
Randomly adjust brightness, contrast, sa: Randomly adjust brightness, contrast, saturation, and hue of the image. Applied after resize.
Randomly adjust the sharpness of the ima: Randomly adjust the sharpness of the image. Complements Gaussian blur by also allowing images to become sharper, improving robustness to varying image quality. Applied after resize.
Randomly convert the image to grayscale. Forces the model to learn shape and texture features rather than relying solely on color information. Applied after resize.
Randomly crop images based on Intersecti: Randomly crop images based on Intersection over Union (IoU) criteria. Applied before resize. Note: this augmentation is not supported when tiling is enabled.
Randomly erase a rectangular region in t: Randomly erase a rectangular region in the image and fill it with a constant value. Also known as Cutout. Helps the model learn to rely on broader context rather than specific local features. Applied after resize.
Randomly flip images horizontally along: Randomly flip images horizontally along the vertical axis (swap left and right). Applied after resize.
Randomly flip images vertically along th: Randomly flip images vertically along the horizontal axis (swap top and bottom). Applied after resize.
Randomly resize and crop the image. Appl: Randomly resize and crop the image. Applied instead of resize. When disabled, a standard resize to the target input size is used instead. Note: this augmentation is not supported when tiling is enabled.
Randomly zoom out the image by placing i: Randomly zoom out the image by placing it on a larger canvas with padding. Applied before resize.
Range (min, max) of aspect ratios to app: Range (min, max) of aspect ratios to apply during resize crop operation. Aspect ratio is defined as width divided by height. For example, (0.75, 1.33) allows the crop to have an aspect ratio between 3:4 and 4:3.
Range (min, max) of brightness adjustmen: Range (min, max) of brightness adjustment factors. A random factor from this range will be multiplied with the image brightness. For example, (0.8, 1.2) means brightness can be reduced by 20% or increased by 20%.
Range (min, max) of contrast adjustment: Range (min, max) of contrast adjustment factors. A random factor from this range will be multiplied with the image contrast. For example, (0.5, 1.5) means contrast can be halved or increased by up to 50%.
Range (min, max) of crop ratios to apply: Range (min, max) of crop ratios to apply during resize crop operation. Specifies the fraction of the original image dimensions to retain after cropping. For example, (0.8, 1.0) will randomly crop between 80% and 100% of the original size. Both values should be between 0.0 and 1.0.
Range (min, max) of hue adjustment value: Range (min, max) of hue adjustment values. A random value from this range will be added to the image hue. For example, (-0.05, 0.05) means hue can be shifted by up to ±0.05.
Range (min, max) of saturation adjustmen: Range (min, max) of saturation adjustment factors. A random factor from this range will be multiplied with the image saturation. For example, (0.5, 1.5) means saturation can be halved or increased by up to 50%.
Range (min, max) of scaling factors to a: Range (min, max) of scaling factors to apply during affine transformation. Both values should be > 0.0. For example, (0.8, 1.2) will randomly scale the image between 80% and 120% of its original size.
Range (min, max) of sigma values for Gau: Range (min, max) of sigma values for Gaussian blur. Sigma controls the amount of blurring. A random value from this range will be used for each image.
Range (min, max) of the aspect ratio of: Range (min, max) of the aspect ratio of the erased area. For example, (0.3, 3.3) allows the erased rectangle to have varying proportions.
Range (min, max) of the proportion of th: Range (min, max) of the proportion of the image area to erase. For example, (0.02, 0.33) means erasing between 2% and 33% of the image area.
Range (min, max) of the zoom-out scale f: Range (min, max) of the zoom-out scale factor for each side. The image will be placed on a canvas scaled by a random factor from this range. For example, (1.0, 4.0) means the canvas can be up to 4x the original image size. The minimum value must be >= 1.0.
Scale factor for the random perspective: Scale factor for the random perspective crop applied after mosaic assembly. The random scale is sampled from [1 - scale, 1 + scale]. Higher values produce more aggressive zoom variation.
Size of each tile in pixels. Decreasing: Size of each tile in pixels. Decreasing the tile size typically results in higher accuracy, but it is also more computationally expensive due to the higher number of tiles. In any case, the tile must be large enough to capture the entire object and its surrounding context, so choose a value larger than the size of most annotations.
Size of the Gaussian kernel. Larger kern: Size of the Gaussian kernel. Larger kernel sizes result in stronger blurring. Must be a positive odd integer.
Split images into overlapping tiles for: Split images into overlapping tiles for processing, useful for detecting small objects.
Standard deviation of the Gaussian noise: Standard deviation of the Gaussian noise. Controls the intensity of the noise. Higher values result in noisier images.
Strategy used to transform pixel intensi: Strategy used to transform pixel intensities. 'Unit interval scaling' divides by max_intensity_value, thus mapping the range [0, max_intensity_value] to [0, 1]. 'Windowing' isolates a specific intensity range, mapping a specific window (specified with center and width) to [0, 1] and clipping values outside the window. 'Range scaling with clipping' multiplies pixel values by a scale factor, clips the result to a specified range (clip_min_value, clip_max_value) and finally normalizes to [0, 1].
Subset split parameters define how the d: Subset split parameters define how the dataset is divided into training, validation, and test subsets. The training subset is used to fit the model, the validation subset is used to estimate the prediction error during training and the test subset is used to evaluate the final performance of the model. The percentages for training, validation, and test subsets must sum to 100.
The learning rate scheduler adjusts the: The learning rate scheduler adjusts the learning rate during training according to a predefined schedule or based on validation performance, helping to improve convergence and training stability.
Toggle to enable or disable early stoppi: Toggle to enable or disable early stopping during training.
Toggle to enable or disable gradient acc: Toggle to enable or disable gradient accumulation during training.
Toggle to enable or disable gradient cli: Toggle to enable or disable gradient clipping during training.
Toggle to enable or disable the LR linea: Toggle to enable or disable the LR linear warmup phase at the beginning of training.
Translate fraction for the random perspe: Translate fraction for the random perspective crop. The crop centre shifts by up to +/- translate * image_size pixels. Higher values allow more positional variation.
Type of learning rate scheduler to use d: Type of learning rate scheduler to use during training. With ReduceLROnPlateau, the learning rate will be reduced by a predetermined factor when the validation metric stops improving. With CosineAnnealing, the learning rate will follow a cosine decay schedule, gradually decreasing over the course of training.
Weight decay is a regularization techniq: Weight decay is a regularization technique that adds a penalty to the loss function based on the squared magnitude of the model weights (L2 regularization). It helps prevent overfitting by discouraging large weight values.
Whether to apply maximum annotation obje: Whether to apply maximum annotation objects filtering
Whether to apply minimum annotation obje: Whether to apply minimum annotation objects filtering
Whether to apply minimum annotation pixe: Whether to apply minimum annotation pixels filtering
Whether to use adaptive tiling based on: Whether to use adaptive tiling based on image content
Width of the intensity window for 'windo: Width of the intensity window for 'windowing' mode. The effective range is [center - width/2, center + width/2], mapped linearly to [0, 1].
Width size in pixels for model input ima: Width size in pixels for model input images. Determines the horizontal resolution at which images are processed.

ATSS (Adaptive Training Sample Selection: ATSS (Adaptive Training Sample Selection) is an anchor-based object detection algorithm that introduces an adaptive strategy for selecting positive and negative samples during training. Instead of using fixed IoU thresholds, ATSS dynamically determines positive samples based on the statistical characteristics of object candidates for each ground truth. This improves training stability and enhances detection performance, especially for objects of varying sizes and aspect ratios.
D-FINE is a powerful real-time object de: D-FINE is a powerful real-time object detector that redefines the bounding box regression task in DETRs as Fine-grained Distribution Refinement (FDR). Combined with the DEIM adaptive augmentation scheduling framework (enabled by default), it achieves outstanding performance with faster convergence.
DINOv2 is a self-supervised vision trans: DINOv2 is a self-supervised vision transformer model trained with a combination of discriminative and generative pretraining objectives. It produces robust, general-purpose visual features that transfer well to classification tasks. Fine-tuning uses DoRA (Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation) for parameter-efficient training, making it especially effective for small-dataset regimes.
DINOv3-DETR is an efficient end-to-end o: DINOv3-DETR is an efficient end-to-end object detection transformer that leverages the DEIMv2 training framework with a DINOv3 backbone, achieving strong accuracy with fewer parameters.
EdgeCrafter detection model (ECDet-L) co: EdgeCrafter detection model (ECDet-L) combines an efficient ECViT backbone with a hybrid encoder and transformer decoder for real-time, high-accuracy object detection with low latency.
EdgeCrafter detection model (ECDet-M) co: EdgeCrafter detection model (ECDet-M) combines an efficient ECViT backbone with a hybrid encoder and transformer decoder for real-time, high-accuracy object detection with low latency.
EdgeCrafter detection model (ECDet-S) co: EdgeCrafter detection model (ECDet-S) combines an efficient ECViT backbone with a hybrid encoder and transformer decoder for real-time, high-accuracy object detection with low latency.
